candidates.tagline: Nothing unveiled its 'AI-first' device — it's one big button
candidates.story: Nothing (the phone maker behind Phone 2 and Phone 3) teased its first 'AI-native product' on November 10, 2026: a handleless brushed-metal rectangle with two pill-shaped LEDs and one large rectangular button with a red dot, described as a screenless 'productivity tool' — launching December 2026 — with pundits already comparing it to a 1970s dictaphone.
candidates.why_funny: A company famous for making phones beautiful with transparent backs and glowing LED strips unveils its vision for the AI future: an object that looks exactly like an old tape recorder.
candidates.alt: Top portion of a small dark-grey brushed-metal device with two pill-shaped LED lights and one large light-grey rectangular button with a prominent red dot in the center

candidates.tagline: San Diego's self-driving future forgot to leave a charger for the humans
candidates.story: Since Waymo launched its autonomous taxi service in San Diego in September 2026, its vehicles have been hogging public fast-charging stations, with human EV drivers reporting waits of up to an hour while multiple Waymo robotaxis occupy every available stall; Waymo says it tries to avoid clustering but builds its own depots 'as operations mature.'
candidates.why_funny: Self-driving vehicles were designed to solve transportation problems — they've now created a new one by outcompeting the humans they're supposed to serve for the same scarce public chargers.
candidates.alt: A white Waymo autonomous Jaguar I-Pace vehicle with the company's distinctive multi-sensor dome on the roof, parked on a city street in San Francisco
